track_problems: eval 10 blue_cup (frame 32), cause judged 'both': the projection sits slightly toward the lower right. It misses the upper-left rim and the left marker ball and spills about 10 px (about 13% of the visible cup height) onto the holding hand. A small shift or tilt is the reviewer's reading, on top of the mesh's wall hole.

eval 32 blue_cup (frame 0), cause unclear: a red skirt about 35 px wide flares 10-15 px past the cup's base onto the thumb and table, and a 2-4 px strip of the upper-left wall is uncovered. The skeptic rejected a uniform pose shift because the rim and right wall fit closely. This may be mesh shape at that end rather than pose.

eval 30 mini_sweeper (frame 224), cause unclear: the overlay stops 5-7 px short of the visible bristle tips (about half the visible bristle strip) and tilts about 3-5 degrees down-left. The hand hides most of the body, so pose and mesh cannot be separated.
eval 3 wooden_spoon (frame 297), cause unclear, negligible: a 2-3 px uncovered sliver along the bowl's left and lower-left edge, with the rest aligned within 1-2 px.
overall: Tracking is in good shape. In all 36 eval pairs the mesh landed on the right object, in the right place and at the right size. Only three pairs (the blue cup in eval 10 and 32, the sweeper in eval 30) show a small offset that might come from the pose. The weak point is the meshes. The wooden spoon, in 10 of the 36 pairs, is good. The white pot, blue cup and dish rack, 16 pairs between them, all have large holes: the pot and the rack are missing most of their floors, and the blue cup has a big hole near its open end and is not round. The beige cup is the worst mesh, two separate pieces with no opening, but it appears in only two episodes. Suggested order of work: the blue cup first, because it is the only one with a measured fix (the thin-wall lathe took it from 0.523 to 0.291 cm on public episodes, though it needs depth from several eval frames); then the pot, the rack and the beige cup. The lathe's gain on any object other than the blue cup, and every other method listed, is an untested hypothesis until measured on public episodes. This review looked at one frame per pair, so it does not catch tracking errors in other frames.
